newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 27.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 27.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Thursday:

* On Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average closed down 55.03 points at 6,983.18 after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan warned that the stock market might be too strong and said the central bank was ready to raise interest rates to ward off inflation.

* A legislative committee of Massachussets is to take up debate on a measure that seeks not only to bar companies from doing business with Massachusetts if they do business with Indonesia, but also calls for the state to divest its pension funds of all Indonesian assets. If the measure becomes law, it will force Massachusetts Treasurer Joe Malone to divest the public pension funds, now totalling more than $18 billion, of all Indonesian holdings.
MARKET

* On Wednesday, the Jakarta Composite Index rose 11.30 points, or 1.61 percent, to close at 712.61 points, the new all time-high in the bourse on sustained buying interest almost across the board, brokers said.
* On Thursday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,391/92.0 at 0200 GMT, compared with Wednesday's closing of 2,389.0/89.5.
STOCKS TO WATCH
* Conglomerate Bimantara Citra on a report that its South Korean partner Hyundai Motor Co had agreed on a $400 million joint venture to make sedans in Indonesia.
* Timber firm Barito Pacific on market speculation that business tycoon Muhammad "Bob" Hasan would acquire a stake in the company through his paper producer PT Kiani Kertas.

* Holding company Bakrie & Brothers on market talk that it would set up a consortium with some Indonesian businessmen and Bank Bumiputera Bhd of Malaysia to help the troubled privately-owned Bank Pacific.
* State-controlled Tambang Timah following its annual general meeting and press conference on Thursday which were scheduled to held at 0300 and 0500 GMT respectively.
* Cigarette maker Sampoerna following its annual public presentation on Thursday at 0300 GMT.
* Indosat after J.P. Morgan raised its rating to "buy" from "long-term buy" on the telecommunications stock.
* Indofood on news reports that analysts were mixed on the implications from its proposed rights issue.
* Budi Acid Jaya on reports that its 1996 profits would be higher than analysts' forecasts.
* Indorama after announcing its 1996 results and forecast of higher profits in 1997.

* Car maker Astra International on a media report last Friday that the company and its Japanese principal had discussed Indonesia's national car policy and increasing local content in Astra-produced vehicles.
* Retailer Multipolar and Hero Supermarket on speculation the Lippo Group had targeted Hero for a takeover or possible link-up, despite company denials.
Also on recent reports that the founder of retailer Matahari, Hari Darmawan, was planning to raise his stake in Multipolar, which recently acquired a controlling 50.1 percent interest in Matahari.
